title: TRAINING INSTITUTES FOR CAPFs
body_text:
A total number of 83 Training Institutions of Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) have been established all over the Country.
Expansion, modernization and upgradation of training centres are being done on requirement basis. Further, purchase of motor vehicles, technical gadgets and creation of manpower for imparting training in CAPFs has been carried out from time to time.
It has been decided to establish Central Jungle Warfare College (CRPF) in Bijapur district, Chhattisgarh and Regional Training Centre (CISF) in Kishanganj district, Bihar.
This was stated by the Minister of State in the Ministry of Home Affairs Shri Nityanand Rai in a written reply to a question in the Lok Sabha.

enrichment.summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply, MoS Home Affairs Nityanand Rai stated that 83 Training Institutions of Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) have been established across India, with ongoing expansion, modernization and upgradation of these centres including procurement of vehicles and technical gadgets. The government has also decided to set up a Central Jungle Warfare College (CRPF) in Bijapur, Chhattisgarh, and a Regional Training Centre (CISF) in Kishanganj, Bihar.
enrichment.context:
CAPFs — comprising CRPF, BSF, CISF, ITBP, SSB and Assam Rifles — are central to India's internal security architecture, handling counter-insurgency, border management, anti-Naxal operations, and critical infrastructure protection. Training infrastructure is a recurring policy focus because CAPFs face challenges of specialized terrain (jungle, high-altitude, riverine) and evolving threats (Left Wing Extremism, cross-border infiltration, urban terrorism), requiring continuous skill upgradation.

The proposed Central Jungle Warfare College in Bijapur is significant because Bijapur lies in the heart of the Bastar region, one of the most Left Wing Extremism (LWE)-affected areas in India, where CRPF personnel conduct sustained anti-Naxal operations. A dedicated jungle warfare training facility here aims to better equip forces for guerrilla-style combat in dense forest terrain, complementing existing facilities like the CRPF's Counter Insurgency and Jungle Warfare (CIJW) school in Kanker. Similarly, the CISF Regional Training Centre in Kishanganj, Bihar addresses the force's expanding mandate beyond public sector undertakings to airports, metro systems, and other critical infrastructure, necessitating decentralized training capacity closer to deployment regions in the eastern states.

This reflects the broader government approach of matching training infrastructure to operational and geographic needs rather than a one-size-fits-all model, and ties into larger internal security modernization efforts under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

prelims_questions.question: The proposed 'Central Jungle Warfare College' mentioned in a recent Ministry of Home Affairs statement is to be established for which Central Armed Police Force, and in which state?
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, the Central Jungle Warfare College is being established for CRPF in Bijapur district, Chhattisgarh, a region significant for anti-Naxal operations.

prelims_questions.question: Which of the following is NOT typically classified as a Central Armed Police Force (CAPF) under the Ministry of Home Affairs?
prelims_questions.explanation: The Indian Coast Guard functions under the Ministry of Defence, not as a CAPF; CRPF, CISF, and BSF are among the recognized Central Armed Police Forces under MHA.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of specialized training infrastructure, such as jungle warfare colleges, in enhancing the operational effectiveness of Central Armed Police Forces in Left Wing Extremism-affected regions.
Examine the evolving role of Central Armed Police Forces beyond traditional border management, and the implications for their training and deployment strategy.
